newsitem.title: USA: Florida sites reject former KKK leader's speech.
newsitem.headline: Florida sites reject former KKK leader's speech.

text.p: At least two sites in Tampa said Thursday they have rejected bookings made by a neo-Nazi group that wants to host a May 10 speech by David Duke, the former Ku Klux Klan leader and former Louisiana state representative.

On Wednesday, board members of Tampa's Firemen's Benevolent Association held an emergency meeting and voted to cancel a rental contract with the National Alliance, a West Virginia-based group that advocates white supremacy, a spokesman for the firemen's group said.

The National Alliance is headed by William Pierce, who wrote "The Turner Diaries," a novel describing a bloody white supremacist takeover of the United States that was found in Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh's car after McVeigh's arrest, an FBI agent testified on Monday.

A Marriott hotel in Tampa, where the group tried to schedule the Duke speech after the firemen's hall cancelled, also cancelled the event Wednesday night after learning more about the National Alliance.

"We don't take a stance on speakers ... But if they have a precedent for violence or we think there is potential for any kind of violent demonstration then we're going to cancel it," Joe Collier, director of sales and marketing for Marriott hotels in Tampa, said.

Flyers distributed to promote Duke's speech said he planned to speak on affirmative action and illegal immigration and quoted him as saying nonwhite births threaten the heritage of white Americans, the Tampa Tribune reported Thursday.
He participated in a debate last fall in California on the anti-affirmative action measure Proposition 209, drawing rock-throwing protesters and riot police.
